# Inside the Achilleús restoration: what the marks recover
Every name in this series was once flattened to fit a keyboard. **Achilleús** is what the evidence put back.

Son of the mortal Pēleús and the sea-goddess Thetis, Achilleús stands exactly between god and man: the strongest argument the Greeks ever made that excellence cannot cancel mortality. His mother Thetis told him he carried two fates: stay at Troy and win glory that never dies, or sail home to a long life forgotten.  In Iliad 9 he weighs them aloud — the first hero in Western literature to choose knowingly, and to choose the flame over the ember.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Achilleús
- **ASCII form:** achilleus
- **Meaning:** "Possibly 'grief of the people' (from ἄχος + λαός), or a pre-Greek name"
- **Domain of influence:** War, Glory, Rage
- **Pantheon:** Greek
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** Ἀχιλλεύς
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 4 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **Ἀχιλλεύς**. On the evidence, it means "Possibly 'grief of the people' (from ἄχος + λαός), or a pre-Greek name".

Strip **Achilleús** to *achilleus* and one piece of evidence vanishes:

- **u → ú** — Stress mark (acute/tone): the stress position the ASCII form cannot show.

None of these marks is decoration. Each one is a fact about how the name was spoken, and each one is checkable against the scholarly record the temple cites.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Achilleús** lives at [/sites/achilleus/](/sites/achilleus/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/achilleus/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/achilleus/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/achilleus/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Achilleús** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Defense, Military & Security** — The Iliad’s first word is his wrath; the short, bright life of imperishable glory is war’s oldest heroism.
- **Sports, Fitness & Competition** — Swift-footed and best of the Achaeans; the pursuit of kléos — imperishable glory — is competition’s oldest prize.
- **Gaming, Fantasy & Entertainment IP** — Hero of the original war epic; the rage-and-glory archetype of combat IP.

This is the part of the file that surprises people: a four-thousand-year-old name, mapping cleanly onto twenty-first-century trades. The patterns are not marketing — they are the same myths, read forward.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Greek tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Theogony](/texts/theogony/), [Homeric Hymns](/texts/homeric-hymns/), and [Works and Days](/texts/works-and-days/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.

This is one of 271 Restoration Files — a second dispatch from every flagship temple in the fleet. The temple's [first dispatch](/sites/achilleus/blog/) tells the founding story of the name; the [blog index](/blog/) holds the whole archive.
